evidence.reference_title: MutS homolog 4 localization to meiotic chromosomes is required for chromosome pairing during meiosis in male and female mice.
evidence.snippet: Our results show that MSH4 localization on chromosomes during the early stages of meiosis is essential for normal chromosome synapsis in prophase I and that it acts in the same pathway as MSH5.

evidence.reference_title: MSH4 acts in conjunction with MLH1 during mammalian meiosis.
evidence.snippet: These results suggest that MSH4 is first required for chromosome synapsis and that this MutS homologue is involved later with MLH1 in meiotic reciprocal recombination.

nodes.description: Raised FSH is the laboratory finding that defines POI; it is also raised in the milder diminished ovarian reserve presentation.

nodes.description: Homozygous donor splice-site variant in a Colombian family; exon 17 skipping removes the Walker B motif of the ATPase domain.

evidence.reference_title: A homozygous donor splice-site mutation in the meiotic gene MSH4 causes primary ovarian insufficiency.
evidence.snippet: Exon trapping experiments showed that the splice-site mutation induced skipping of exon 17. At the protein level, the mutation p.Ile743_Lys785del is predicted to lead to the ablation of the highly conserved Walker B motif of the ATP-binding domain, thus inactivating MSH4.

nodes.description: Infertility, including failed in vitro fertilization from poor oocyte quantity and quality.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of compound heterozygous variants in MSH4 as a novel genetic cause of diminished ovarian reserve.
evidence.snippet: The patient presented with poor oocyte quantity and quality, resulting in unsuccessful in vitro fertilization cycles.

evidence.reference_title: A novel homozygote nonsense variant of MSH4 leads to primary ovarian insufficiency and non-obstructive azoospermia.
evidence.snippet: The results show that the testicular sperm retrieval and ovarian stimulation cycles have not been successful yet.

nodes.description: There is no MSH4-directed therapy. As for other causes of POI, estrogen with progestogen replaces ovarian hormones to limit the bone, cardiovascular and other consequences of early estrogen loss; it does not restore fertility, for which donor oocytes are the usual option. The progestogen is bound as progesterone because the ChEBI progestogen class is a role term that the agent slot does not admit; other progestogens are equally used.

evidence.reference_title: Evidence-based guideline: Premature Ovarian Insufficiency.
evidence.snippet: Although hormone therapy (HT) can mitigate some of these effects, many questions still remain regarding the optimal management of POI.

evidence.reference_title: A homozygous donor splice-site mutation in the meiotic gene MSH4 causes primary ovarian insufficiency.
evidence.snippet: Our study describes the first MSH4 mutation associated with POI and increases the number of meiotic/DNA repair genes formally implicated as being responsible for this condition.

evidence.reference_title: MSH4 and MSH5 variants in premature ovarian insufficiency: A literature review and case study.
evidence.snippet: Biallelic MSH4 variants are well-established causes of POI and non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA), with MSH4 recognised as a high-evidence gene on clinical panels.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic landscape of a large cohort of Primary Ovarian Insufficiency: New genes and pathways and implications for personalized medicine.
evidence.snippet: We confirmed the causal role of BRCA2, FANCM, BNC1, ERCC6, MSH4, BMPR1A, BMPR1B, BMPR2, ESR2, CAV1, SPIDR, RCBTB1 and ATG7 previously reported in isolated patients/families.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic screening in patients with ovarian dysfunction.
evidence.snippet: The splice-site variants in SYCE1 and MSH4 affected canonical splicing isoforms, leading to missing protein domains or premature termination.

nodes.description: Biallelic MSH4 variants remove or disrupt the MSH4 protein, most often in its C-terminal ATPase domain, inactivating the MSH4-MSH5 (MutS-gamma) heterodimer that recognizes and stabilizes Holliday junction recombination intermediates in meiotic prophase I.

evidence.reference_title: A homozygous donor splice-site mutation in the meiotic gene MSH4 causes primary ovarian insufficiency.
evidence.snippet: Exon trapping experiments showed that the splice-site mutation induced skipping of exon 17.

evidence.reference_title: Rare missense variant in MSH4 associated with primary gonadal failure in both 46, XX and 46, XY individuals.
evidence.snippet: Along with its heterodimer partner MSH5, it is responsible for double-strand Holliday junction recognition and stabilization, to ensure accurate chromosome segregation during meiosis.

evidence.reference_title: MutSγ-Induced DNA Conformational Changes Provide Insights into Its Role in Meiotic Recombination.
evidence.snippet: Similar to the human protein, Sc Msh4-Msh5 exhibits the highest affinity for the HJ with a Kd < 0.4 nM in solution.

nodes.description: Targeted disruption of Msh4 causes sterility of both sexes with failed homolog pairing and synapsis in meiotic prophase I.

Loss of oocytes depletes the ovarian follicle pool. Depending on residual reserve, women present with amenorrhea and premature ovarian insufficiency, or with diminished ovarian reserve and poor oocyte yield and quality in assisted reproduction.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of compound heterozygous variants in MSH4 as a novel genetic cause of diminished ovarian reserve.
evidence.snippet: Our findings indicate a correlation between MSH4 variants and reduced oocyte quality, as well as abnormal morphology of the first polar body, thereby expanding the phenotypic spectrum associated with MSH4 variants.

evidence.reference_title: MutS homolog 4 localization to meiotic chromosomes is required for chromosome pairing during meiosis in male and female mice.
evidence.snippet: As in the case of Msh5−/− females, the loss of the oocyte pool resulted in the disruption of ovarian development and the complete loss of ovarian structures in the adult Msh4−/− female.

nodes.description: Cessation of ovarian function before age 40 is the defining feature in 46,XX carriers of biallelic MSH4 variants.

evidence.reference_title: A homozygous donor splice-site mutation in the meiotic gene MSH4 causes primary ovarian insufficiency.
evidence.snippet: Our study describes the first MSH4 mutation associated with POI

evidence.reference_title: Bi-allelic variants in DNA mismatch repair proteins MutS Homolog MSH4 and MSH5 cause infertility in both sexes.
evidence.snippet: Additionally, we detected biallelic variants in MSH4 in two men with MeiA and in the sister of one proband with POI.

nodes.description: Most affected women have menarche followed by loss of menses.

evidence.reference_title: MSH4 and MSH5 variants in premature ovarian insufficiency: A literature review and case study.
evidence.snippet: Affected individuals predominantly present with secondary amenorrhoea, with emerging evidence for milder phenotypes, including diminished ovarian reserve (DOR).

nodes.description: Homozygous nonsense variant creating a stop codon at residue 40, in an Iranian family with affected siblings of both sexes.

evidence.reference_title: A novel homozygote nonsense variant of MSH4 leads to primary ovarian insufficiency and non-obstructive azoospermia.
evidence.snippet: WES analysis of the proband uncovered a novel homozygote nonsense variant, namely c.118C>T in MSH4. This variant resulted in the occurrence of a premature stop codon in residue 40 of MSH4.

nodes.description: Compound heterozygous genotype in a woman with menarche at 19 and POI diagnosed at 31, with the two alleles inherited from different parents.

evidence.reference_title: Next-generation sequencing of 500 POI patients identified novel responsible monogenic and oligogenic variants.
evidence.snippet: A compound heterozygous variant in MSH4 (p.M740fs and p.T792A) was identified in POI-63, who had spontaneous menarche at 19 years of age and diagnosed with POI at 31 years old. The compound heterozygous variant was confirmed to be inherited paternally and maternally, respectively

nodes.description: Homozygous missense in the MutS signature motif adjacent to the Walker B motif, found in a consanguineous Iranian family with both POI and NOA.

evidence.reference_title: Rare missense variant in MSH4 associated with primary gonadal failure in both 46, XX and 46, XY individuals.
evidence.snippet: Patients with primary ovarian insufficiency (POI) and non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) were homozygous for the rare missense variant p. S754L located in the highly conserved MSH4 MutS signature motif of the ATPase domain.
